description:
## Problem
Nothing in BenchBox can run DIGen, check its output, or tie a result to the exact source files it used. The Databricks project's runner answers DIGen's licence prompt automatically and splits and rewrites generated files; neither is acceptable here.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- 2026-11-21, generator: "We will ship any needed assets with BenchBox and include the sourcing and upstream license conditions for our users to review and consider". Clarified the same day: the TPC-DI tools exactly as the TPC distributes them (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration), unmodified, inside the BenchBox package, with the TPC licence, the PDGF licence, the legend and a sourcing file; BenchBox runs them with the user's Java; no generator code is ported or rewritten. Source: "The official archive you place at ~/Developer/tpc-tools/, with SHA-256 recorded."
- 2026-11-21, licence acknowledgement: no flag; on every generation print "TPC-DI data is generated by the TPC's DIGen tool, which includes bankmark's PDGF. Read the licence conditions in {path}." and continue.
- 2026-11-21, Java message: "TPC-DI data generation needs Java {versions}. Set JAVA_HOME or put a supported java on PATH. Found: {found}."
- 2026-11-21, supported Java: "Whatever versions the early check shows to work." (The owner's clarification of the tools decision said "the user's Java 8"; this later answer widens it to what is shown to work.)
- 2026-11-21, scale: keep smallest publishable 3 and default 5 (list 3, 5, 10, 100). Below 3: "The run is allowed; the result is marked not validated with the reason, and publication and the validator refuse it."
- 2026-11-21, names approved: result block `benchmark.tpcdi` with `source.provider = "digen"`, `audit.engine = "sut"` (or `"duckdb-export"` for DataFrame mode), `etl.base = "databricks-tpc-di@8e0f944"`; timed rows `TDI_HISTORICAL`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_1`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_2`; JVM options override `BENCHBOX_TPCDI_JAVA_OPTS`. "If an existing BenchBox convention requires a different spelling, the implementer uses it and lists the change in the pull request."
- 2026-11-21, approved to run on this machine through the heavy-work lock with output under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`: DIGen (once the archive is placed); a clone of the DuckDB implementation at a pinned commit; a JDK 8 downloaded into `~/Developer/tpc-tools/` (not system-wide) if none is installed.
- 2026-11-20: generation runs under the optional run time limit (`--timeout`), which needs run-timeout step 1b.

## Change
Add `benchbox/core/tpcdi/sources/digen.py` and wire it to the `generate` phase. It finds Java through `JAVA_HOME` then `PATH`; checks the version against the supported set; prints the licence notice with the path of the shipped licence files; runs the shipped DIGen as a child process through `run_child` so the run time limit and descendant clean-up apply, with JVM options from `BENCHBOX_TPCDI_JAVA_OPTS`; answers DIGen's own licence prompt only after the notice has been printed, and records in the result that the notice was shown; checks that `Batch1`, `Batch2`, `Batch3` and `digen_report.txt` exist; parses the row counts the metric needs (historical and both incremental) from the report; writes a staging manifest (SHA-256 per file) and refuses to continue if staging later differs from it (Clause 2.4.5). Scale: default 5, list 3, 5, 10, 100; any whole number from 3 up may be run. A scale below 3 or a fractional scale is refused before Java starts with the owner's message: "TPC-DI data generation needs a whole-number scale factor of 3 or more. Got: {sf}." It runs the tools from the cache directory the tools step unpacks into. It writes run-timeout step 1b's in-progress marker so a generation that was ended is never reused as complete. Replace the `tpcdi` entry in `utils/datagen_version.py` with a key on the tools' SHA-256 and the scale factor so cached old data is never reused. The Databricks project's `digen_runner.py` is a design reference only (order of pre-flight checks); no code is copied.

## Decision gates
Owner action first: the owner places the official `TPC-DI_Tools_v1.1.0.zip` and the separate Appendix archive (specification page 117) under `~/Developer/tpc-tools/`. This item stays blocked until both are there. The archives are never committed as archives. The early check on the owner-action item (DIGen at scale 3 twice) has already shown which Java works and whether output is deterministic; extend it here to each Java version installed on this machine and to scale 5. The supported set is exactly the versions shown to work, listed in the pull request with the evidence. If DIGen is not deterministic, stop and report: the manifest and the comparison steps depend on it. If DIGen's prompt cannot be answered without pretending the user typed it, describe the mechanism in the pull request before arming. Any option or configuration key name not in the approved names list follows existing convention and is listed in the pull request.

## Verification rubric
Pass: unit tests with the child process replaced: Java absent, Java unsupported (exact message), notice printed with a real path, report parsed, manifest written, tampered staging refused, cache key changes when the tools hash or scale changes, the run time limit ends the child. Real runs through `make heavy-run` at scale 3 and 5, twice each: identical manifests; times and sizes in the pull request. `git diff --stat` shows no DIGen output. The CLI still refuses TPC-DI (the quarantine step's test still passes). `make pr-preflight` passes. Also by test: the printed notice equals the owner's text with a path that exists; the result records that the notice was shown; `BENCHBOX_TPCDI_JAVA_OPTS` reaches the child's command line; scale 2 and scale 3.5 are refused with the owner's message before any child process starts; a generation ended part-way leaves the in-progress marker and is not reused.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message, label text or name (option, configuration key, result field, file name, test hook) the owner has not already chosen is chosen by the implementer following existing BenchBox conventions and the specification, and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). Texts the owner has chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) are used verbatim.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. Delivery follows the batch plan on tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120: a batch member ends at a landing report and its batch has one final pull request; a serial item has its own pull request.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in `_sources/tpc-di/`, `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/` and `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/tools/`. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- Owner, 2026-11-21: "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step." The catalogue is `DEPARTURES.yaml`; every entry of the comparison's expected-differences list must cite a catalogue row. After the milestone stop, a new catalogue row in which BenchBox follows the specification is listed in the pull request; a row that would keep behaviour of the Databricks project that departs from the specification stops for the owner's approval (owner, 2026-11-21).
- The agent never contacts bankmark, the TPC or the Databricks project's author.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
